# Hard stops (HS-v1)

These apply to every session, every role, every card. If a step would cross
one, stop the step, write what was needed in your return file with status
`BLOCKED`, and do nothing else for that step.

- **HS-1 Live data.** Never open, list, read, copy, back up, restore or
  query the live Apunta data folder, its backups, the owner's Claude export
  or Halaxy PDFs. Never contact port **7717**. Never run
  `scripts/recover-current-linux.mjs` or `scripts/smoke-live.mjs`.
- **HS-2 Isolation.** Every command that starts an Apunta server, opens a
  database or launches the app runs through `scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs` once
  card P0.3 is APPROVED. Before that, only non-launching edits and unit
  tests that use in-memory or temporary databases created by the test.
- **HS-3 Downloads.** Only items in `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md`, by the rules
  there. Never pull an Ollama tag that already exists locally. Never
  remove or replace an Ollama model.
- **HS-4 Git.** Work only on `feature/v2`, starting from the base commit the
  coordinator gave you. Never merge into `main`, pull, rebase, reset,
  force-push, rewrite history, or change repository visibility. Stage
  explicit paths only.
- **HS-5 Secrets.** Never create, print, copy or commit a production
  signing key or password. Test keys live only inside a sandbox run folder.
- **HS-6 Network at runtime.** No new network access from `server/`, `web/`
  or `shared/`. The only runtime exceptions are model acquisition (existing)
  and the update check in the Tauri shell (contract C-UPD).
- **HS-7 Safety instruments.** Never loosen a scorer, guard, lock, test or
  threshold to make a result pass. Never change a threshold in
  `docs/v2/CONTRACTS.md`.
- **HS-8 Fabricated data only.** Fixtures, audio, screenshots and examples
  are fabricated. English uses the prototype's sample people; Spanish uses
  only names in `e2e/fixtures/eval-es/NAMES.md`.
- **HS-9 Protected paths.** Never edit `prototype/`. Never edit files outside
  your card's "May edit" list.
- **HS-10 Owner-only actions.** Never enable Spanish in release builds, write
  the owner's clinical verdict, publish a release, create GitHub secrets, or
  stop or inspect the live v1 instance.

## Fixed decisions
1. **In-house `t()`.** `Intl.PluralRules`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and
   `Intl.NumberFormat` only, no new dependency, and no `npm run licenses` churn.
2. **The catalogue shape, written out**, so two readings cannot both satisfy
   the card. `MessageKey` is `keyof typeof en`; a key is `dotted.case`
   (`notes.count`, `errors.language_unavailable`); placeholders are `{name}` and
   `params` is a flat `Record<string, string | number>`. In `t.ts`:

   ```ts
   export type ParamKind = 'text' | 'number' | 'date' | 'dateOnly';

   export interface Message {
     /** A key with no count: one string, `{name}` placeholders only. */
     text: string;
     /** Present only on a key that takes a numeric parameter (Fixed decision 4). */
     plural?: Partial<Record<Intl.LDMLPluralRule, string>>;
     /** How each `{name}` renders; a name absent here is `text`. */
     kind?: Record<string, ParamKind>;
   }

   export type MessageParams = Readonly<Record<string, string | number>>;
   ```

   `en.ts` ends `export const en = { … } as const satisfies Record<string, Message>;`
   and `t.ts` derives `export type MessageKey = keyof typeof en;`.
   `es-MX.ts` ends `export const esMX = { … } satisfies Record<MessageKey, Message>;`
   — so a key missing from es-MX, or a key it does not have in English, is a
   `tsc` error and nothing else. The two files export the values; `t.ts` exports
   `t`, `Message`, `MessageKey` and `ParamKind`; `shared/src/index.ts`
   re-exports `t`, `MessageKey` and both catalogues.
3. **Placeholder names must match, and a test says so.** For every key, the set
   of `{name}` tokens in the English entry equals the set in the es-MX entry —
   compared per entry at runtime, because a type cannot see inside a string.
4. **Plurals.** A key that takes a numeric parameter (`count`, `days`, … — the one declared with `kind: 'number'`) carries a per-category form map, never a
   hand-rolled `count === 1`, and the category is
   `Intl.PluralRules(locale).select(count)`. The floor is `one` and `other` in
   `en` and `one`, `many` and `other` in `es-MX` — three cardinals, because
   `Intl.PluralRules('es-MX').resolvedOptions().pluralCategories` is exactly
   `many, one, other` on this box (ICU 78.3). A category the catalogue omits
   falls back to `other`, so `en` needs no `many` entry. That numeric parameter is also the key's
   `number` param, so `1,000,000` renders through `Intl.NumberFormat` and takes
   es-MX's `many` form.
5. **Dates and numbers.** Each key declares how each of its parameters renders
   through `kind`: `text` inserts the string; `number` goes through
   `Intl.NumberFormat(locale)`; `dateOnly` takes a `YYYY-MM-DD` string parsed
   field by field into a local `Date` — never `new Date(iso)`, which reads a
   bare date as UTC midnight and renders as the day before west of Greenwich —
   and formats it in the local zone; `date` takes an ISO timestamp and formats
   it in the local zone. Both date kinds use the one option set
   `{ month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' }` that
   `format.ts:20-24` uses, so `2026-08-08` is `Aug 8, 2026` in `en` and
   `8 ago 2026` in `es-MX` (S1.4 §2.1's day–month–year order, verified on this
   box). Number grouping is whatever `Intl` says: `Intl.NumberFormat('es-MX')`
   gives `1,234` on this box, which differs from S1.4 §2.3's prose
   recommendation of a space (`1 234`); `Intl` wins here, the difference is
   recorded as a finding for **S2.7**/**S2.8**, and no test hardcodes a
   separator — each asserts against `Intl.NumberFormat(locale).format(n)`.
6. **The English-unchanged rule, and its oracle.** The English value of each
   seed key equals what the app produces today for the same input, and the seed
   table below names the function each key is pinned to. `web/src/lib/format.ts`
   and `web/src/lib/plural.ts` are that oracle and are read-only for this card:
   no line of either changes. The seed pins `format.ts:34`, `:59-61`, `:90`,
   `:105`, `plural.ts:2-4` and `BackupCard.tsx:180`; `formatShortDate` (`:75`),
   `formatDayGap` (`:111`) and `formatRelativeTime` (`:119`) are the oracles
   S2.3 to S2.5 pin their keys to when they extract those strings — no seed key
   is invented for them here.
7. **Runtime fallbacks.** An unknown key, or a `{name}` the entry expects and
   `params` does not carry, **throws** in a test build and returns the **English**
   string otherwise — never the raw key, never an empty string, never
   `undefined`. The strict read is `process.env['VITEST'] === 'true'` behind a
   `typeof process !== 'undefined'` guard, which vitest sets
   (`vitest@4.1.11`) and the browser bundle never does. A parameter the entry
   does not name is **ignored**, not an error: `params` is a flat bag and a
   caller may pass more than one entry needs. Every one of these is a case in
   `t.test.ts`.
8. **The seed catalogue — nine keys, fixed here** as S1.1 fixed its tables, so
   the parity, plural, date and English-unchanged cases are writable and a
   reviewer can check them against something. The `es-MX` strings follow S1.4's
   recommendations (`tú` per O-1, sentence case per §2.4, `copia de seguridad`
   per §3.3); **S2.7**/**S2.8** own any later change to this copy, so a copy
   review is not read as a card defect. The sample name is the prototype's.

   | key | `kind` | English | es-MX | pinned to |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `brand.name` | `text` | `Apunta` | `Apunta` (never translated) | `BrandWordmark.tsx:34`; S1.4 §3.4 |
   | `notes.title` | `text` | `Notes` | `Notas` | `NotesColumn.tsx:41` |
   | `notes.count` | `count`: `number`, plural | one: `{count} note`; other: `{count} notes` | one: `{count} nota`; many: `{count} notas`; other: `{count} notas` | `format.ts:59-61`; `plural.ts:2-4` |
   | `notes.today` | `text` | `Today` | `Hoy` | `format.ts:34` (the same-day case) |
   | `notes.date` | `day`: `dateOnly` | `Aug 8, 2026` from `2026-08-08` | `8 ago 2026` | `format.ts:90` `formatPlanDate` |
   | `note.updatedAt` | `at`: `date` | `Aug 8, 2026` from a local timestamp | `8 ago 2026` | `format.ts:105` `formatInstantAsDate` |
   | `backup.stale` | `days`: `number`, plural | one: `No backup for over {days} day.`; other: `No backup for over {days} days.` | one: `No hay copias de seguridad de hace más de {days} día.`; many: `No hay copias de seguridad de hace más de {days} días.`; other: same as `many` | `BackupCard.tsx:180` with `BACKUP_STALE_DAYS` |
   | `brainstorm.empty` | `name`: `text` | `Think out loud about {name} — this conversation is never written into their notes.` | `Piensa en voz alta sobre {name}: esta conversación nunca se escribe en sus notas.` | `BrainstormView.tsx:175-178` with `format.ts:16-18`; `{name}` is `John` |
   | `errors.language_unavailable` | `text` | `Español is not available in this build of Apunta. Choose English, or install the Spanish edition.` | `El español no está disponible en esta versión de Apunta. Elige inglés o instala la edición en español.` | `settings.test.ts:149`, byte for byte |

   The es-MX half covers every category the rules need: a plural with three
   cardinals, a date-only value, a timestamp, a grouped number, a named
   placeholder, a code-style key and the untranslated brand.
9. **Server-facing messages: the mechanism here, the list in S2.5.** Codes plus
   parameters, with the catalogues mapping code to text and logs staying English
   and content-free. The namespace is reserved now: **every** code key is
   `errors.<code>`, `MessageKey` covers both namespaces (UI keys and codes in
   one union, so one parity rule and one placeholder test guard both), and the
   seed demonstrates the mapping with `errors.language_unavailable` — the code
   C-LANG@1 rule 1 already requires and S2.1 already added to the closed
   `ApiErrorCodeSchema` — whose English text is the message the server sends
   today. **S2.5** owns the rest of the code list; the return file records that
   owed sentence with the paths it will edit.
10. **Mounting is not this card's, and the gap is named.** `web/src/App.tsx:38-42`
    is where `SettingsProvider` is mounted, and no card in S2 is licensed to
    touch it. **S2.3** owns the mount: it is the first card whose components
    call `t()`, and it needs the provider above the router, beside
    `SettingsProvider`; the coordinator adds `web/src/App.tsx` (the import and
    the wrapper element, no string) to S2.3's May edit, and **S2.6** (Language
    control, `<html lang>`) depends on it. Until that amendment lands this card
    delivers an unmounted provider, and its own rows are provider-level, not
    App-level: `i18n.test.tsx` mounts the two providers itself, and the row that
    proves the *real* tree follows the `language` setting belongs to S2.3.
    Record the owed sentence in the return file naming `web/src/App.tsx`, S2.3
    and S2.6. Mounting the provider here instead is a stop condition, not a
    quiet widening.
11. **`check-ui-strings.mjs`'s CLI contract**, which S2.3 V2 and S2.4 V1 already
    invoke:
    - the **bare** invocation is **report-only and exits 0** in this card. S2.4
      flips the bare default to failing and leaves `--report` report-only.
    - `--report` forces report-only, whatever the bare default is.
    - an optional **path argument** restricts the scan, so S2.3's V2 can be
      scoped to the files it owns; with no argument the scan is `web/src`.
    - `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx` and `web/src/test/` are excluded, as S1.4's
      enumeration excluded them (§3.1; 36 test files live under `web/src`
      against 51 non-test `.tsx`).
    - the report prints **one line per offending file** with `file:line` and the
      literal, then a final `TOTAL <n>` line — so V2's "the literal count" is
      checkable and S2.3's scoped expectation is readable off a per-file
      breakdown.
    - a **literal** is what S1.4's enumerator took: JSX text nodes plus the
      `placeholder`, `aria-label`, `title` and `alt` string attributes, parsed
      with the TypeScript compiler API the way
      `docs/v2/evidence/S1.4/evidence.md` Appendix A does. An interpolated
      `{expr}` inside JSX text is not itself a literal (the pieces around it
      are), a template literal is not scanned, and the two classes S1.4 §3.6
      deliberately gave no entry of their own (symbols and separators, sentence
      fragments) are not reported.
    - the **allowlist** is `scripts/check-ui-strings.allow.json`: a **sorted JSON
      array of exact strings**, matched whole. Its seed entries are the ten
      keep-as-is tokens of S1.4 §3.4 — `Apunta`, `Claude`, `Halaxy`, `SKILL.md`,
      `ICD-10-CM`, `DSM-5-TR`, `NPI`, `PDF`, `Mac`, `MXN` — which is what
      absorbs `aria-label="Apunta"` at `BrandWordmark.tsx:34`.
    - the report-only default is **not** an HS-7 loosening, and it is not a
      licence to keep it: S2.4's switch to failing is a card of its own, and
      turning the checker failing here to quiet a red lint is HS-7.

The case is the negative one the card's headline guardrail needs: it builds a `mkdtemp` tree shaped like `web/src` (removed in `afterAll`, nothing written inside the checkout), holding **one JSX text literal, one `aria-label`, one `title`, one `placeholder`, one `alt`** and the allowlisted token `Apunta`; runs `node scripts/check-ui-strings.mjs --report <that path>`; and asserts each of the four non-allowlisted literals is reported once with `file:line` and its text, that `Apunta` is **not** reported, and that the documented `--report` exit code is 0. A checker that scans nothing, ignores the four attributes, or matches everything fails this row — which is the point: V2 alone can be satisfied by a script that prints `0` and exits 0 |
| V4 | `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/apunta-node/node-v24.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH" && npm run lint && npm run typecheck` | exit 0. `lint` now ends in the bare `node scripts/check-ui-strings.mjs`, which is report-only here, so it contributes output and never a non-zero exit — a red lint from that step means the default was flipped, which is S2.4's switch and is HS-7 if it was done to quiet a row. `typecheck` is where the **type-level** parity lives: `shared/src/i18n/*.test.ts` carries a `// @ts-expect-error` case for a key `es-MX` is missing, and `tsc` is the only thing that can see it (`shared/tsconfig.typecheck.json` includes `src/**/*.ts` with `exclude: []`, and `web/tsconfig.json` includes `src/**/*.tsx`); an unused `@ts-expect-error` is itself an error, so the case cannot be vacuous |

All four rows run on this box as written. Every row exports the provisioned Node
first, because the root `engines` is `>=24.19.0 <25` (`package.json:8-10`, E1)
and the box default is **v26.8.2** — outside it, and V1 goes red for a reason no

3 of the 6 cases in `web/src/lib/appearance.test.ts`
(`docs/v2/state/reviews/P0.5-impl.md:121-132`). Nothing here launches anything:
every row is in-process vitest, a `node` script over the working tree, eslint,

so, as in AM-025, the rows run bare rather than through

and no `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`, no `npm run e2e --workspace @apunta/e2e
--` form and no `--grep` appears above**; the dispatch's sandbox port stays

## Stop conditions
- A seed string that cannot be expressed as one key plus parameters is
  **reported** with its location, not concatenated and not split into two keys
  to make it fit. Two-direction strings such as `formatDayGap`'s
  `in 12 days` / `12 days ago` are the known case; S2.3 owns them.
- The provider needs a mount to be reachable at all (`web/src/App.tsx`), or the
  catalogues need an export surface beyond the one `shared/src/index.ts` line
  licensed here: a `BLOCKED` return naming the file and the coordinator
  amendment it would take, not a quiet widening of May edit. Fixed decision 10
  is the shape of the first; the second is the same answer as S2.1's
  `server/src/http/errors.ts` stop condition.
- A `tsc` error in a file this card does not own, or any other red assertion in
  one (the Node 26 `appearance.test.ts` case above is the known one, and V1
  exports Node 24 to avoid it), is a `BLOCKED` return with the compiler or
  runner output. Do not make a field optional to quiet the compiler, and do not
  relax an assertion (HS-7).
- The bare checker default would have to become failing for any row to go green:
  stop. That switch is S2.4's, and making it here to quiet lint is HS-7.
- `Intl`'s output for a locale contradicts S1.4's prose recommendation (the
  `es-MX` thousands separator is the known case): record it as a finding for
  S2.7/S2.8 in the return file and ship `Intl`'s. Do not hand-format a number to
  match the prose.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-LANG@1 Language, documents and jobs

**Built by** S2.1. **Proven by** S2.6, S4b.1, S5.6. **Consumers:** web,
server routes, AI prompts, guards, speech, spell check, formats, backup.

1. Setting `language` ∈ `en` | `es-MX`, default `en`. The server exposes
   `spanishAvailable: boolean`: true only when `APUNTA_DEV_SPANISH=1` (D12).
   When false, the Language control is hidden and `es-MX` is rejected by
   `PUT /api/settings` with code `language_unavailable`.
2. Locale mapping (one table in `shared/src/i18n/locales.ts`):

   | App | UI and `Intl` | Whisper `-l` | Speech model | Dictionary | Prompts |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `en` | unchanged from today | `en` | `ggml-tiny.en.bin` | current English | current |
   | `es-MX` | `es-MX` | `es` | per C-STT selection | per S1.5 | Spanish set |

3. Documents: migration adds `locale TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en'` to notes
   and to formats. **All existing rows are `en`.** New notes take the job's
   locale. Existing notes and formats are never translated or relabelled.
4. Jobs capture `{ locale, sttModel, llmModel, promptSet }` at start
   (recording, transcription, draft, refine, plan, briefing, brainstorm).
   Retries, SSE and persistence use the captured context, never the current
   setting. **Refine uses the target note's locale**, whatever the UI
   language and whatever language the request is typed in.
5. Section roles: `shared/src/section-roles.ts` maps known section names in
   both languages (case- and accent-insensitive) to role IDs (`location`,
   `presentation`, `risk`, `discussion`, `intervention`, `actions`,
   `next_session`, and the SOAP and intake roles). Guards use roles, not
   strings. Unknown sections get role `custom`. Stored strings are not
   rewritten.
6. Changing Language is blocked while any job or save is active: the web
   control is disabled with a reason; the server also returns 409
   `language_change_blocked` if it knows of an active job.
7. Spanish dictation requires the Spanish speech model to be ready (C-ACQ).
   If it is not, dictation shows "Spanish speech model not installed" with
   a download action. **Spanish audio is never sent to the English model.**
8. The Spanish standard format is created as a separate format with
   `locale: 'es-MX'`; English formats are untouched. Imported formats take
   the UI language at import time; the user can change a format's locale.
9. Backups and restores carry the `locale` columns.

**Rejection example.** UI switched to Español, user refines an existing
English note with a Spanish instruction → the note stays English, the reply
explains the change in the note's language.

## C-SETTINGS@1 Settings mutations

**Built by** P1.1. **Proven by** P1.1 and S2.6. **Consumers:** every
settings control, including Language.

- `SettingsProvider` exposes `update(patch)`. It applies the patch to the
  provider's state immediately (optimistic), then calls `putSettings`.
- Each key has a sequence number. A response for an older sequence than the
  latest request for that key is ignored (last intent wins).
- On failure: the provider restores the value from before **that** request
  for the failed keys only, and the control shows the existing error
  message style.
- No control keeps a persisted setting in local component state as its
  source of truth. Local state is allowed only for in-progress text input.
- Radio groups follow native radio keyboard behaviour: arrow keys move and
  select within the group; Tab enters at the selected option.

**Normal example.** Dark → choose Light → navigate to Home → back to
Settings **without reload** → Light selected, page light, provider value
light; after reload, still light.

**Rejection example.** Save fails → value returns to Dark, page returns to
dark, error shown; no reload claims Light.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.
